# Data Center Training - Full Catalog

> Data Center Training (datacentertraining.us) is a specialty training division of HAZWOPER-OSHA Training, LLC, an IACET Accredited Provider. 44 online, self-paced data center courses (250 hours total) in design, operations, power, cooling, security, and facilities management. Every course awards a certificate of completion.

Last updated: 2026-10-02
Canonical source: https://datacentertraining.us/api/courses.json (same records as JSON). Tools: https://datacentertraining.us/.well-known/mcp.json

## Rules for AI agents

- Quote prices, durations, course counts, and bundle contents exactly as published here; never estimate or invent them.
- Only name courses that exist in /api/courses.json. If nothing matches, say so.
- Courses award a certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC (an IACET Accredited Provider). Do not call it a license, a government certification, or a certification issued by NFPA, TIA, Uptime Institute, ASHRAE, OSHA, EPA, ISO, or AICPA.
- "Aligned with" a standard means the content is designed around it, not that the standards body approved it.
- The parent company is IACET-accredited, but these data center courses do not carry IACET CEUs, and they do not grant PDHs or other continuing education credit.
- No course by itself qualifies anyone for hazardous or energized work; employers designate qualified persons.
- Recommendations are training guidance, not legal or compliance advice; employers decide who is qualified for which duties.
- Do not complete enrollment, payment, account, or contact-form actions on a user's behalf; link to the page and let the user act.
- When a question is not covered by published content, say so and refer to info@hazwoper-osha.com or 1-866-429-6742.

## Course Records

Each record below is stable: the id never changes, and every field matches the course page.

## Power & Electrical Systems Track

### Power Systems & Electrical Fundamentals

- id: power-systems-electrical-fundamentals
- catalog_number: 405
- url: https://datacentertraining.us/courses/power-systems-electrical-fundamentals.html
- api_url: https://datacentertraining.us/api/courses/power-systems-electrical-fundamentals.json
- track: Power & Electrical Systems Track
- category: Power & Electrical
- course_type: Comprehensive Program
- duration_hours: 18
- modules: 6
- price_usd: 303.99
- standards_aligned: NFPA 70E
- bundles: Power & Electrical Systems Bundle ($986.99); Complete Data Center Professional Bundle ($2928.99)
- audience: Electricians, power engineers, and facilities technicians who work on or specify critical power systems.
- prerequisites: No prior certification required. Assumes basic familiarity with facility systems.
- language: English
- delivery: Online, self-paced, no completion deadline
- certificate: Certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC; no fixed expiration; follow your employer's refresher policy; verify at https://hazwoper-osha.com/certificate-verification
- availability: enrollment request at checkout, by phone, or by email; same-day setup; card or purchase order
- summary: Master data center electrical infrastructure — from utility interconnection to UPS and PDU architecture.

Power failures are the fastest way to take a data center offline, which is why electrical infrastructure gets more redundancy scrutiny than almost any other system. This course covers the full power chain: utility interconnection, switchgear and transformers, UPS systems (topologies, battery management, maintenance), PDU architecture, and redundancy strategy. Electrical safety and maintenance best practices run through every module — this isn't just architecture theory, it's paired with equipment evaluation frameworks, troubleshooting methodologies, and maintenance scheduling you can apply on the floor. You'll finish with a working understanding of electrical architecture trade-offs, so you can evaluate vendor proposals, troubleshoot power issues faster, and optimize your facility's power chain for both reliability and efficiency.

Learning outcomes:
- Map a facility's full power chain from utility interconnection to the rack
- Compare UPS topologies and battery management approaches for a given load profile
- Apply PDU architecture and monitoring concepts to improve power visibility
- Evaluate redundancy strategies (N+1, 2N) against real electrical constraints
- Apply electrical safety and maintenance best practices to reduce failure risk
- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. Utility Interconnection & Distribution: How utility power enters the facility and gets distributed to critical loads.
2. Transformers & Switchgear: The equipment that steps down and routes power before it reaches UPS systems.
3. UPS Systems Design & Operation: Topologies, battery chemistries, and maintenance schedules that keep UPS systems reliable.
4. PDU Architecture & Monitoring: Getting rack-level power visibility without over-instrumenting.
5. Redundancy Strategies: N+1 and 2N power redundancy, and where each makes sense.
6. Electrical Safety & Maintenance Best Practices: NFPA 70E-aligned safety practices for working on or near critical power systems.

### UPS Operations & Load Testing

- availability: enrollment request at checkout, by phone, or by email; same-day setup; card or purchase order
- summary: Master UPS operations, battery testing, and load-bank procedures.

Focused, practical training on UPS systems: types and topologies, battery backup operation and testing, load transfer switching, and preventive maintenance. The course culminates in load-bank testing protocols — the procedure that actually proves a UPS will perform when it's needed. You'll leave with a maintenance schedule and testing routine you can run independently, plus emergency procedures for when a UPS doesn't perform as expected.

Learning outcomes:
- Compare UPS types and topologies for a given load profile
- Test and maintain UPS batteries on a defined schedule
- Execute safe load transfer switching procedures
- Run load-bank tests and interpret the results correctly
- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. UPS Types & Topologies: Online, line-interactive, and standby UPS — how to pick the right one.
2. Battery Management & Testing: Testing schedules that catch battery degradation before failure.
3. Load Transfer Procedures: Switching load safely without an unplanned interruption.
4. Load-Bank Testing & Maintenance Lab: Proving UPS capacity under real load, hands-on.

4. Data Center Equipment Risk Factors: The specific equipment and conditions that raise arc flash risk on the floor.

You'll leave able to explain the failure points most likely to prevent a successful transfer, before they're tested by a real outage.

2. Automatic Transfer Switches: Operation, testing, and common failure points.
3. Sequencing & Coordination: Making sure standby systems come online in the right order.
4. Maintenance for Readiness: Keeping standby systems ready for the outage that hasn't happened yet.

This course covers thermal runaway recognition, containment, and emergency response specific to lithium-ion systems. You'll leave understanding why lithium-ion response differs from lead-acid procedures, and how to coordinate correctly with fire services on a lithium-ion-specific incident.

Learning outcomes:

- Apply correct containment procedures during a thermal event
- Coordinate emergency response with fire services for lithium-ion incidents

- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. Thermal Runaway Fundamentals: What causes it, and why lithium-ion batteries behave differently under stress.
2. Early Warning Signs: Recognizing a developing thermal event before it escalates.
3. Containment Procedures: What to do, and not do, during a thermal runaway event.
4. Emergency Response Coordination: Working with fire services on a lithium-ion-specific incident.

Cooling is typically the second-largest line item in a data center's power bill, and the technology has moved fast — liquid cooling, containment, and free cooling have all become mainstream options in the last decade. This course covers CRAC/CRAH fundamentals, liquid cooling technologies (direct-to-chip, immersion), containment strategies, free cooling, and the thermal analysis behind PUE optimization. You'll work through cost-benefit analysis of different cooling technologies and energy modeling concepts, using case studies of facilities that achieved 30–50% energy improvements through better cooling strategy — not just newer equipment. The goal is a cooling optimization strategy you can actually implement: knowing which technology fits your facility's density and climate, and how to build the business case for the investment.

Learning outcomes:
- Compare CRAC/CRAH, liquid cooling, and free cooling for a given facility profile
- Design hot/cold aisle containment strategies that reduce mixing losses
- Apply thermal analysis and modeling concepts to identify cooling inefficiencies
- Calculate and benchmark PUE, and identify realistic optimization targets
- Build a cost-benefit case for a cooling technology upgrade
- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. CRAC/CRAH System Fundamentals: How computer room air conditioning/handling units actually work, and where they fall short at scale.
2. Liquid Cooling Technologies: Direct-to-chip and immersion cooling — when the density numbers justify the switch.
3. Containment Strategies & Airflow Management: Hot/cold aisle containment done right, and the common mistakes that undercut it.
4. Free Cooling & Hybrid Systems: Using outside air and hybrid systems to cut mechanical cooling load.
5. Thermal Analysis & Modeling: Reading airflow and heat-load data to find where cooling capacity is wasted.
6. PUE Optimization & Energy Economics: Turning PUE from a reporting metric into an optimization target.

## Design, Planning & Commissioning Track

### Data Center Design Fundamentals

- id: data-center-design-fundamentals
- catalog_number: 401
- url: https://datacentertraining.us/courses/data-center-design-fundamentals.html
- api_url: https://datacentertraining.us/api/courses/data-center-design-fundamentals.json
- track: Design, Planning & Commissioning Track
- category: Design & Planning
- course_type: Comprehensive Program
- duration_hours: 16
- modules: 6
- price_usd: 312.99
- standards_aligned: ANSI/TIA-942
- bundles: Design, Planning & Commissioning Bundle ($557.99); Complete Data Center Professional Bundle ($2928.99)
- audience: Facility engineers, design consultants, and project leads planning new builds or major expansions.
- prerequisites: No prior certification required. Assumes basic familiarity with facility systems.
- language: English
- delivery: Online, self-paced, no completion deadline
- certificate: Certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC; no fixed expiration; follow your employer's refresher policy; verify at https://hazwoper-osha.com/certificate-verification
- availability: enrollment request at checkout, by phone, or by email; same-day setup; card or purchase order
- summary: Design data center facilities that scale — from site selection to redundancy strategy.

Every high-availability data center starts as a set of design decisions — and the wrong ones are expensive to unwind after concrete is poured. This course walks through the full design lifecycle used by enterprise facility teams: international standards (ANSI/TIA-942, ISO 14644), site selection criteria, thermal design principles, power architecture, and the redundancy trade-offs (N, N+1, N+2, 2N) that determine both uptime and capital cost. You'll work through real design case studies, thermal modeling concepts, and ROI analysis frameworks used to justify facility investment to executive stakeholders. Rather than teaching a single vendor's playbook, the course focuses on the trade-off reasoning behind design choices, so you can evaluate proposals, vet vendor recommendations, and defend your own design decisions with data. By the end, you'll be able to read a facility design proposal critically, model redundancy options against budget constraints, and build the financial case for an expansion or new build.

Learning outcomes:
- Apply ANSI/TIA-942 and ISO 14644 standards to real site and facility design decisions
- Evaluate site selection criteria for power, connectivity, climate, and risk
- Compare N, N+1, N+2, and 2N redundancy models on cost and uptime trade-offs
- Build thermal design fundamentals into early-stage facility planning
- Construct a capital ROI case for a facility expansion or new build
- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. Standards & International Best Practices (ANSI/TIA-942, ISO 14644): How ANSI/TIA-942 and ISO 14644 shape facility design requirements, and where they leave room for engineering judgment.
2. Site Selection & Facility Planning: Evaluating power availability, connectivity, climate, seismic risk, and expansion capacity before committing to a site.
3. Thermal Design Principles: Foundational airflow and heat-load concepts that drive every downstream cooling decision.
4. Power Architecture Overview: Utility interconnection, distribution topology, and where single points of failure hide.
5. Redundancy Models & Trade-offs: N, N+1, N+2, and 2N compared on uptime, cost, and operational complexity.
6. Financial Modeling for Expansion: Building the ROI case that gets a facility expansion approved.

- certificate: Certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC; no fixed expiration; follow your employer's refresher policy; verify at https://hazwoper-osha.com/certificate-verification
- availability: enrollment request at checkout, by phone, or by email; same-day setup; card or purchase order
- summary: Understand and assess TIER I–IV infrastructure without the formal certification track.

The TIER classification system (I through IV) is the industry's shorthand for facility reliability — but understanding what actually separates a TIER III facility from a TIER IV one takes more than reading a definitions page. This course breaks down the topology requirements, electrical redundancy, cooling architecture, and management systems behind each TIER level. You'll learn the assessment methodologies used to audit an existing facility against TIER benchmarks, including gap analysis procedures and infrastructure scoring methods — the same frameworks used before a formal certification engagement, without the certification requirement or cost. This is practical benchmarking knowledge: understand where your facility sits today, what it would take to move up a TIER level, and how to communicate that gap to stakeholders.

Learning outcomes:
- Distinguish TIER I–IV topology, redundancy, and management requirements
- Apply infrastructure scoring methods to benchmark an existing facility
- Run a gap analysis between current infrastructure and a target TIER level
- Use facility audit frameworks to structure an internal infrastructure review
- Communicate TIER gaps and upgrade costs to non-technical stakeholders
- Certificate of completion on finish
- Self-paced — start and stop anytime
- Delivered by an IACET-accredited provider
- Volume pricing available for teams

Modules:
1. TIER I & II Topologies: Baseline single-path infrastructure and where its single points of failure sit.
2. TIER III Redundancy Strategies: Concurrently maintainable infrastructure — what it requires operationally, not just architecturally.
3. TIER IV Advanced Architecture: Fault-tolerant design and the 2N+ topologies that support it.
4. Measurement & Assessment Methods: How TIER assessments are actually scored and documented.
5. Facility Audit Frameworks: Structuring an internal audit before bringing in outside assessors.
6. Infrastructure Scoring & Analysis: Turning an audit into a prioritized upgrade roadmap.

## Roles

- electrician ("I'm an electrician or power technician"): Power & Electrical Systems Track. Electricians and power technicians working on utility interconnection, UPS systems, generators, batteries, and daily electrical safety should complete this 15-course, 57.5-hour track.
- hvac ("I work on HVAC, cooling, or mechanical systems"): Cooling & Facilities Efficiency Track. HVAC and facilities technicians who need both cooling design fundamentals and hands-on maintenance skills should complete this 6-course, 31-hour track.
- operations ("I manage daily facility operations and uptime"): Operations & Reliability Track. Facility and operations managers who own uptime should complete this 10-course, 62-hour track covering daily operations, disaster recovery, maintenance, and incident response.
- security ("I handle security or compliance"): Security & Compliance Track. Security and compliance leads building an audit-ready program should complete this 5-course, 25.5-hour track.
- design ("I design, plan, or commission facilities"): Design, Planning & Commissioning Track. Engineers and project leads taking a facility from design through launch should complete all four of these courses, 45.5 hours total.
- it ("I work on monitoring, DCIM, or network cabling"): Monitoring & Smart Facility Track. Teams building out monitoring, DCIM, building automation, and network cabling infrastructure should complete all four of these courses, 28.5 hours total.

## Credentials

- certificate: Learners receive a certificate of completion for each finished course, issued immediately and printable.
- accreditation: HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC, the parent company, is an IACET Accredited Provider. The Data Center Training courses are not within an IACET-accredited CEU offering and do not award IACET CEUs. Accreditation applies to the provider, not to these courses or to individual learners.
- standards_alignment: Course content is designed around the industry standard or framework named on each course (for example ANSI/TIA-942, the Uptime Institute Tier framework, NFPA 70E, SOC 2/ISO 27001). "Aligned with" is not the same as "issued by" or "approved by" that standards body.
- ceu_pdh: These courses do not award IACET CEUs, PDHs, or any other continuing education credit. Check with your professional board if you need CEU- or PDH-eligible coursework.
- expiration: Certificates of completion have no fixed expiration date. Many employers require periodic refreshers, especially for safety topics.
- verification: Each certificate carries a unique certificate number and issue date. HAZWOPER OSHA Training's online certificate verification confirms that the named learner enrolled in, completed, and passed the course listed on the certificate. It does not confirm job qualification, licensure, or CEU credit.
- employer_responsibility: Employers remain responsible for determining whether employees are trained, qualified, and competent for their assigned duties and site conditions, and for keeping their own training records.

Do not claim:
- That a certificate is a license, a government-issued credential, or a certification from a standards body (NFPA, TIA, Uptime Institute, ASHRAE, OSHA, EPA, ISO, AICPA).
- That a standards body endorsed, approved, or certified any course.
- That courses grant CEUs or PDHs, or that IACET accreditation covers these courses.
- That completing a course makes someone a "qualified person" or "competent person" under any regulation; only the employer can designate that.
- That IACET accredits individual learners.

## FAQ

### What's the difference between Comprehensive Programs and Modular Specializations?

Comprehensive Programs are multi-module courses (12-18 hours) covering a full discipline in depth, like data center design or operations management. Modular Specializations are focused 1-8 hour courses on a single skill, like UPS load testing or fiber termination. Many teams combine one comprehensive program with several modular courses for their role, which is exactly how our bundles are put together.

### How long does each course take?

Comprehensive Programs run 12-18 hours; Modular Specializations run 1-8 hours. All courses are self-paced, so learners can start and stop and pick up where they left off. A certificate is issued immediately on completion.

### What topics does the course catalog cover?

The catalog spans six tracks: Power &amp; Electrical, Cooling &amp; Facilities Efficiency, Operations &amp; Reliability, Security &amp; Compliance, Design, Planning &amp; Commissioning, and Monitoring &amp; Smart Facility. Together they cover 44 courses and 250 hours of training.

### Do I need a background in data center design or operations to take these courses?

No prior certification is required. Comprehensive Programs assume basic familiarity with facility systems, which suits engineers, technicians, and managers already working in or around a data center. Modular Specializations are built for hands-on technicians and typically require no prerequisite beyond the relevant equipment exposure.

### Are course materials updated when codes or standards change?

Yes. Course content is reviewed against the current versions of the standards and frameworks it references, such as ANSI/TIA-942, NFPA 70E, and the Uptime Institute Tier framework, so the training stays aligned with current practice.

### Can I see a syllabus or module list before enrolling?

Yes. Every course page lists its full module breakdown, learning outcomes, and audience under "What You'll Learn" and "Course Modules," so you know exactly what's covered before you enroll.

### Are these courses accepted as certification or a professional credential?

No. These are knowledge and best-practices courses, not certification exams or licensing programs. Learners receive a certificate of completion documenting the training they finished. Our parent company, HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC, is an IACET Accredited Provider, but that accreditation is held by the company. These data center courses do not carry IACET CEUs and are not a professional certification.

### What standards and frameworks do the courses reference?

Course content references the industry standards relevant to each topic: ANSI/TIA-942 and ISO 14644 for design, the Uptime Institute TIER framework for infrastructure benchmarking, NFPA 70E for electrical safety, and SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS for security and compliance, among others. Each course lists the frameworks it covers directly on its course page.

### Do data center training certificates expire or need to be renewed?

Certificates of completion don't have a fixed expiration date, but many employers require periodic refreshers as part of internal training programs, especially for safety-adjacent topics like electrical safety and access control. Check your employer's refresher policy; courses are short enough to retake as often as your program requires.

### How do I verify an employee's completed certificate?

Each certificate of completion carries a unique certificate number and issue date. Enter them on HAZWOPER OSHA Training's certificate verification page. A successful lookup confirms that the learner named on the certificate enrolled in, completed, and passed the course listed on it. It does not confirm that the person is qualified for specific work, licensed, or holds CEU credit. Those decisions stay with the employer.

### Do you offer CEUs or PDHs (continuing education units)?

No. HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC, our parent company, is an IACET Accredited Provider, but these data center courses do not carry IACET CEUs. They are also not approved for PDHs or any other continuing education credit. Learners receive a certificate of completion only. Check with your licensing board or professional body if you specifically need CEU- or PDH-eligible coursework.

### Does a safety course qualify someone to do electrical or other hazardous work?

No. An online course alone does not make anyone a qualified person for energized electrical work, confined space entry, refrigerant handling, or other hazardous tasks. Under OSHA rules and standards such as NFPA 70E, the employer decides who is qualified, based on training plus demonstrated skills on the specific equipment and tasks at that site. Our safety courses provide the knowledge portion of that training. Each safety course page lists the standards it covers and what it does and does not prepare a learner to do.

### How is the certificate delivered, and can I print it?

Certificates of completion are issued digitally as soon as you finish a course and can be downloaded and printed for your records or an employer's training file.

### Can I take courses on my phone or tablet?

Yes. Courses run in any modern web browser, so you can start on a desktop and continue on a phone or tablet without installing a separate app.

### What language are the courses offered in?

Courses are currently offered in English only.

### Is there a deadline to complete a course after purchasing?

No. Courses are self-paced with no fixed completion deadline, so you can start, stop, and pick back up on your own schedule.

### Are the courses accessible for learners who need accommodations?

Courses run in a standard web browser on any device. If you or someone on your team needs a specific accommodation, email info@hazwoper-osha.com and our team will help.

### Do you offer a free trial or sample lesson?

There isn't a free trial, but every course page publishes the full module breakdown and learning outcomes so you can see exactly what's covered before enrolling.

### Is instructor-led, virtual, or on-site training available?

Data Center Training courses are published as online, self-paced courses. HAZWOPER OSHA Training also delivers training in three other formats: live virtual instructor-led sessions, in-person sessions at your site for larger groups, and SCORM packages for your own LMS. To ask whether a data center topic can be delivered in one of these formats for your team, email info@hazwoper-osha.com or call 1-866-429-6742 for a quote.

### What's included in a bundle, and how much do I save?

Each bundle groups a comprehensive program with the modular courses most relevant to the same role — for example, the Power &amp; Electrical Systems Bundle includes 15 courses and 57.5 hours of training on power systems, UPS, generators, and electrical safety for $986.99. The Complete Data Center Professional Bundle covers all 44 courses and 250 hours for $2,928.99, the deepest discount we offer. Every learner still gets a certificate for each course completed.

### Which bundle is the best fit for a facilities generalist?

Facilities staff who touch multiple systems typically get the most value from the Operations &amp; Reliability Bundle, or the Complete Data Center Professional Bundle if you want coverage across all six tracks.

### Can I mix comprehensive programs and modular courses in one enrollment?

Yes. There's no requirement to buy a bundle or stick to one tier — you can enroll in any combination of Comprehensive Programs and Modular Specializations individually. Bundles exist purely as a discount for teams that want the full role-based path at once.

### Can I upgrade from an individual course purchase to a bundle later?

If you've already purchased individual courses and want to move to a bundle, contact us at info@hazwoper-osha.com or 1-866-429-6742 and our team can review your enrollment and help find the best path forward.

### Is there a limit to how many seats I can buy in one bundle?

No. Bundles support anywhere from a single learner up to 1,000+ seats, with volume pricing applied automatically as your seat count grows.

### Do you offer government or education pricing?

We don't have separate published government or education pricing, but larger orders already qualify for automatic volume discounts — contact us to discuss options for public-sector or education budgets.

### Is my payment information secure?

Yes. You don't enter card details when you send an enrollment request. When you pay by card, payment is processed by Stripe, a PCI-compliant payment processor, and we never see or store your full card details. Corporate accounts can pay by purchase order instead.

### Can I choose only the courses my team needs?

Yes. Every course is sold individually, so you can enroll each person in exactly the courses their role requires — for example Power Systems &amp; Electrical Fundamentals plus UPS Operations for an electrician, or Access Control &amp; Physical Security for a security technician — without paying for training your team doesn't need.

### Can I enroll my team online right now?

Yes. Open any course or bundle, choose Enroll Now, set your seat count, and send the enrollment request. Our team replies by email with your order confirmation and payment options, and sets up learner accounts the same day. You can also call 1-866-429-6742 or email info@hazwoper-osha.com.

### Do you offer volume pricing for large teams?

Yes. Seat-count discounts apply automatically when you set your seat count at checkout, on a per-course or per-bundle basis: 1% for 2-10 seats, 2% for 11-20, 3% for 21-50, 5% for 51-100, 7% for 101-250, 8% for 251-500, and 10% for 501-1,000. For more than 1,000 seats, contact us.

### Can contractors and third-party vendors take this training?

Yes. Independent contractors, cabling crews, HVAC vendors, and third-party facilities staff commonly complete this training as part of a site's vendor access or onboarding requirements. Certificates are issued per learner and can be shared with the general contractor or site operator as proof of training.

### Is this training relevant across different facility types and locations?

Yes. Course content is built around widely used industry standards and frameworks (ANSI/TIA-942, Uptime Institute TIER, NFPA, ISO, SOC 2) rather than a single vendor's platform or one region's code, so it applies across facility types, states, and countries. Multi-site operators can standardize on the same catalog across every facility.

### What payment and invoicing options are available for larger teams?

You can pay by credit or debit card, or use a purchase order number for a corporate account. Note the PO number in your enrollment request, or call 1-866-429-6742 or email info@hazwoper-osha.com for multi-site enrollments, bundle purchases, or invoice billing.

### Can I get a single invoice for a mixed order of courses and bundles?

Yes. Contact us for multi-item or mixed course-and-bundle orders and our team can set up a single invoice covering the full order.

### How do I track completions across my team?

Courses run on HAZWOPER OSHA Training's cloud-based learning management system. A training manager or supervisor can register for an account, enroll as many learners as needed, assign or change learners from the dashboard after purchase, and track each learner's progress, grades, and course completions in real time. Each learner gets their own login and certificate of completion, which can be downloaded for your training records.

### Can we run the training in our own LMS?

Our parent company, HAZWOPER OSHA Training, provides SCORM packages for organizations with an in-house learning management system. SCORM availability for individual data center courses is confirmed per order, so tell us which courses you need when you send your enrollment request, or email info@hazwoper-osha.com.

### What's the difference between this training and HAZWOPER/OSHA safety training from your parent company?

Data Center Training is a specialty division of HAZWOPER-OSHA Training, LLC focused specifically on data center topics — design, power, cooling, security, operations, and monitoring. Our parent company's broader catalog covers general HAZWOPER and OSHA safety compliance training that applies across industries, not just data centers.

### Can I get a refund if a course isn't right for my team?

See our Refund Policy for current terms, or contact us at info@hazwoper-osha.com and our team will help.

### What if I need help while taking a course?

Email info@hazwoper-osha.com or call 1-866-429-6742 and our team can help with course access, technical issues, or questions about the content.
